source.extract: source, note and the listed keys only

note: TEST KEYS ONLY. Every private scalar below is derived from the key name as sha256('orch-f1-test-key|' + name) mod (n-1) + 1 and is published on purpose; the signatures are RFC 6979 (deterministic), so consumers verify the stored signature and never re-sign.

transition_cases.name: out_of_band_non_signer_missing_accepted_unpublished
transition_cases.note: learned out of band (another workspace, the relay's feed, the owner): never demanded as completeness evidence; the receiver keeps enforcing it and forwards it for publication

transition_cases.name: chain_learned_non_signer_missing_diverged
transition_cases.note: the same revocation, authenticated in this workspace's accepted history: completeness demands it

transition_cases.name: out_of_band_revocation_of_the_signer_refused_lost
transition_cases.note: C3 applies to every held revocation, whatever its class or reason

transition_cases.name: out_of_band_revocation_of_the_signer_refused_retired
transition_cases.note: C3 applies to every held revocation, whatever its class or reason

transition_cases.name: out_of_band_revocation_of_the_signer_refused_compromised
transition_cases.note: C3 applies to every held revocation, whatever its class or reason

transition_cases.name: chain_lost_local_compromised_carried_lost_accepted_unpublished
transition_cases.note: reasons are tracked separately: the chain-learned lost is carried (complete); the out-of-band compromised upgrade is not, which is the signal, not a refusal

transition_cases.name: out_of_band_retired_carried_lost_accepted
transition_cases.note: lost and retired are equally strong: not weaker, so not unpublished

transition_cases.name: cross_person_revocation_of_the_signer_device_not_refused
transition_cases.note: mara's PK signs a revocation of sev's device id; known_devices is {}, so the receiver knew no binding for sev1 before this restore and first-come admission of mara's evidence is reachable: judge_offer must stay safe on it. It does not refuse the owner's restore, and once accepted the restore's certificate binds sev1 to sev, so the evidence is dropped: not unpublished either

transition_cases.name: same_person_revocation_of_the_signer_device_refused
transition_cases.note: the genuine counterpart of cross_person_revocation_of_the_signer_device_not_refused

transition_cases.name: out_of_band_several_missing_unpublished_sorted_unique
transition_cases.note: local_revocations in descending device-id order, the first device twice (lost and retired)

transition_cases.name: hash_only_withheld_revocation_not_demanded
transition_cases.note: the relay delivers only the head of withheld_event (abandoned_heads); the receiver never inspected its body, so the revocation is not chain-learned (known limit: the policy preserves only revocations the receiver established in accepted history)

transition_cases.name: hash_only_withheld_revocation_held_out_of_band
transition_cases.note: the relay delivers only the head of withheld_event (abandoned_heads); the receiver never inspected its body, so the revocation is not chain-learned (known limit: the policy preserves only revocations the receiver established in accepted history)

transition_cases.name: hash_only_withheld_revocation_chain_learned_diverged
transition_cases.note: the relay delivers only the head of withheld_event (abandoned_heads); the receiver never inspected its body, so the revocation is not chain-learned (known limit: the policy preserves only revocations the receiver established in accepted history)

transition_cases.name: walk_compromised_learned_from_higher_n_bundle_alarm_only
transition_cases.note: learned_later_in_walk comes from a higher-n bundle judged after this one: it is not known_revocations here; the receiver commits this transition and raises an alarm

transition_cases.name: walk_compromised_learned_from_lower_n_bundle_refuses
transition_cases.note: learned from a lower-n bundle of the same walk, so held when this one is judged

transition_cases.name: walk_retired_known_before_sync_stays_refused_until_repaired
transition_cases.note: liveness cost: a genuine older transition by a device the receiver already knows retired stays refused until an owner pairs the receiver again

transition_cases.name: non_owner_revocation_held_ticket_restore_accepted
transition_cases.note: a ticket restore carries [] and cannot deliver a revocation; a non-owner revocation the receiver holds neither completes nor blocks it

transition_cases.name: ticket_restore_out_of_band_revocation_carries_no_unpublished
transition_cases.note: revocation.unpublished is a workspace-restore signal: a ticket restore carries []

transition_cases.name: cross_person_compromised_learned_later_no_alarm
transition_cases.note: mara's compromised revocation of sev's device id, learned later: matched by device and person like the refusal, so no alarm (and, held earlier, no refusal either)

transition_cases.name: walk_lost_learned_from_higher_n_bundle_no_alarm
transition_cases.note: learned_later_in_walk holds a lost revocation of the signer: no alarm (only compromised alarms)

transition_cases.name: restore_tail_missing_and_other_log_conflict
transition_cases.note: two defects: the restore's tail proof is removed and T's workspace entry conflicts with the held one; the restore tail is checked first

transition_cases.name: other_log_conflict_with_restore_tail_present
transition_cases.note: the control of restore_tail_missing_and_other_log_conflict: the same T with the tail proof present
